en.title: Fresh snow in Hintertux next week? A small 14 cm at the top (23–29 November 2026)
en.description: Hintertux gets 14 cm at the top next week (23–29 Nov): a surface refresh on the glacier, not a powder storm. Data from 16 November.
en.lede: Next week in Hintertux is a light dusting, not a reason to book a powder day. From 23 to 29 November the forecast shows 14 cm near the top of the mountain (ranging from 3 to 24 cm) and 12 cm at the base, so the week will freshen the existing snow rather than pile up a deep new layer.

p: The two weeks before 23 November matter more than you might think. From 16 to 22 November, the top gets only 7 cm (4–11 cm range), which is a thin layer. Next week's 14 cm lands on that small base, so the snow is recent but not built up.
On these numbers, the precipitation falls as snow almost everywhere in Hintertux because the site sits high enough that the snow line stays well below the lowest lifts.

The pattern changes little from top to bottom. Near 3000 m you get 14 cm; near 2400 m it is 13 cm; near 1600 m (the base) it is 12 cm. The range at each height is wider: the top could see as little as 3 cm or as much as 24 cm, while the base could get 2 to 22 cm.
This tight spread means the snow is delivered across all elevations fairly evenly. Hintertux is a glacier area that hardly needs a storm to ski; new snow mostly freshens the surface.

The 14 cm is not spread evenly across the week. Wednesday 25 November is the busiest day at the top, with 3 cm forecast and a possible 5 cm at best. Friday 27 brings another 3 cm, and Sunday 29 adds 3 cm and could reach 6 cm. The other days are nearly dry.
If you are hunting fresh snow, Wednesday 25 is the day to be on the Gefrorene Wand glacier slopes, where snow lasts longest and you gain height fastest.

Mayrhofen, 13 km away, gets 17 cm at the top next week. Stubai Glacier, 42 km away, is forecast at 14 cm. Obergurgl, 52 km away, also expects 14 cm. Hintertux itself sits at 14 cm, so it is in the middle of this group rather than standing out.
A few centimetres either way is well within the forecast's own uncertainty, so all four resorts are receiving the same storm system at nearly the same intensity.

sections.h: Where to ski for the best snow
p: The glacier slopes under the Olperer at Gefrorene Wand are your safest bet. They stay open nearly year-round and hold fresh snow because of their height and aspect. Wednesday 25 November, when 3–5 cm arrives, is the time to ski them.

Treat Hintertux village at the foot of the Tux valley as the weak point: snow falls there too, but it settles and hardens faster at lower elevation. By the week's end, the pistes will be softened but not deep.

The gap between the forecast's low case (3 cm at the top) and high case (24 cm) is large. This spread reflects real uncertainty about the storm's exact path and intensity. The first few days of the forecast are more reliable than the end of the week.

With 14 cm at the top as the central number, Hintertux is not the place to plan a powder trip next week. It is the place to enjoy a refreshed glacier surface and stable spring-like skiing on existing snow.

advice: Wednesday 25 November is the best day for fresh snow; ski the Gefrorene Wand glacier slopes early to find the softest surface.
Before any off-piste skiing, check the regional avalanche bulletin of Tirol, especially after the fresh snow arrives.
With 14 cm at the top next week, focus on the piste groomers rather than chasing deep powder in the backcountry.
The glacier area is skiable almost year-round, so do not wait for perfect powder; a 3–5 cm refresh on Wednesday is enough to improve the ride.
Opening dates are set by the resort; SnowScope's forecast only tells you how much snow is coming, not whether lifts are running.
